📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-24-runtime-core-rtc-p95-recurring`
This is occurrence #296 (lifetime count). The last post was 2026-11-22 06:47Z, more than 24h ago.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Vertical App Experience` (`sales` usergroup / `#team-sales-management`, inert)
Playbook: confirm >3s p95 points cluster on the _screenid* resource, and that runtime-core-api has 0 error logs (latency only).
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (2 total): monitor 115456700 `RTC Screen Load has a high p95 latency`, triggered 23:20:20Z and again 23:33:20Z on 11-23. Degraded cycle, so no permalinks.

Root-cause analysis:
  • `p95:trace.aspnet_core.request{env:prod,service:runtime-core-api,resource_name:post_/api/v1/runtime/load/_screenid*}` 23:05-23:50Z: 29 of 270 points over 3s. Peak 13.11s at 23:32:00Z.
  • `service:runtime-core-api status:error env:prod` 23:10-23:45Z: 0 events. Latency only, as documented.
  • *New correlate, one data point:* during the same minutes, rest-api's own SQL p95 on `peer.hostname:sql-prod-2` hit 30.19s at 23:32. Its window median there was 0.45s, and every other prod SQL host stayed at or under 3.2s. runtime-core-api's SQL on sql-prod-2 peaked at 1.43s at 23:31, while methoddbclus1 stayed at 0.04s.
  • rest-api traffic peaked at 13,137 hits/5min at 23:00 (window median 3,324). Its slow (>5s) spans 23:00-23:45Z were dominated by one paged query, `SELECT … FROM viewaccInvoiceLine WITH (nolock) WHERE InvoiceTxnDate >= @p0 AND < @p1 ORDER BY RecordID OFFSET/FETCH` (103 spans). The tagged user-agent was `n8n`. Spans carry no account_name.
  • A Watchdog story on rest-api `GET /api/v{version}/tables/{table}` latency also fired at 23:28Z. The order fits: the rest-api surge (23:00) came before the SQL and RTC spikes (23:16+).
  • Hypothesis: an n8n integration paging through invoice lines via rest-api saturated sql-prod-2, which slowed RTC screen loads for tenants on that cluster. Next fire: check sql-prod-2 rest-api SQL p95 first.

Corroborate independently:
  • DD APM traces (RTC >3s): https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Aruntime-core-api%20%40duration%3A%3E3s&start=1795475100000&end=1795477800000
  • DD APM traces (rest-api >5s): https://app.datadoghq.com/apm/traces?query=service%3Arest-api%20env%3Aprod%20%40duration%3A%3E5s&start=1795474800000&end=1795477500000
  • DD metric (SQL p95 by host): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.sql_server.query&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cservice%3Arest-api&exp_agg=avg&start=1795474800&end=1795477500
  • DD logs (0 errors): https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Aruntime-core-api%20status%3Aerror%20env%3Aprod&from_ts=1795475400000&to_ts=1795477500000&live=false
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/115456700
  • Kibana: not the evidence datasource for this KB (datadog_apm).

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-03-ms-scheduler-api-seriesid-negative-recordid`
This is occurrence #155 (lifetime count). The last post was 2026-11-20 23:23Z, more than 24h ago.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`customer-management` usergroup / `#team-customer-management`, inert)
Playbook: confirm the 'Failed to Get Series Id for record -1' signature in ES. The ratio is historically marginal, so don't over-escalate. The fix is still the missing recordId=-1 guard in SeriesDataProvider.GetSeriesIdAsync.
Open Jira: none (fix_status: proposed)

Source alerts (1 total): monitor 303750093 `[CRM][P1] ms-scheduler-api error rate high`. Warn at 23:37:33Z on 11-23 (3.271% vs 3% warn), recovered 23:44:33Z. Degraded cycle, so no permalinks.

Root-cause analysis:
  • ES `fields.dd_service.keyword:"ms-scheduler-api" AND level.keyword:Error` 23:20-23:50Z: 9 hits. All 9 are exceptions.Message 'Failed to Get Series Id for record -1 in table Activity', with inner 'Invalid attempt to read when no data is present.' and messageTemplate 'Get Series Info failed for recordId -1'. No other error family.
  • Accounts: baymonservalllp 5, mountainelectricllc3 4.
  • Same code-level bug as before, just recurring. Only a marginal rate breach (3.27% vs 3% warn).

Corroborate independently:
  • Kibana (9 hits): https://logstash.method.me/app/discover#/?_g=(time:(from:'2026-11-23T23:20:00Z',to:'2026-11-23T23:50:00Z'))&_a=(query:(language:kuery,query:'fields.dd_service.keyword%3A%22ms-scheduler-api%22%20AND%20exceptions.Message.keyword%3A%22Failed%20to%20Get%20Series%20Id%20for%20record%20-1%20in%20table%20Activity%22'))
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/303750093
  • Run: `python scripts/es_search.py aggregate --query 'fields.dd_service.keyword:"ms-scheduler-api" AND level.keyword:Error' --from 2026-11-23T23:20:00Z --to 2026-11-23T23:50:00Z --field fields.Account.keyword`

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-28-tables-fields-editview-viewgen-failed-after-retry`
This is occurrence #5 (prior: 07-28, 08-02, 08-23 x2). Single tenant: *camcraigconsulting*.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`)
Open Jira: none filed

*What's happening:* a camcraigconsulting user tried to add dropdown fields `CustomAgendaType` / `CustomAgendaStatus` to table CustomAgenda. The dropdown child-table DDL failed: SqlException "Column 'CustomAgendaType' in table 'CustomAgendaType' is of a type that is invalid for use as a key column in an index". The rollback then failed too ("ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN failed because the column does not exist"), and the spider metadata for those fields stayed committed. Every later field save on CustomAgenda now fails at view regen with `Invalid column name 'CustomAgendaStatus' / 'CustomAgendaType'`. CustomEventSchedule has the same orphan (`CustomEventScheduleType`). The user is blocked editing those tables until the metadata is repaired.

Root-cause analysis (run this cycle):
  • DD APM `trace.aspnet_core.request.errors{env:prod,service:tables-fields} by {resource_name}` 14:00-15:08Z: 11 errors, 100% `post_/v1/field/savefieldlegacyextended` (vs ~2,036 hits; low volume trips the 1% warn)
  • ES `fields.dd_service.keyword:"tables-fields" AND level.keyword:"Error"` 14:35-15:10Z: 74 hits. Table View Creation Failed 26 | EditView ViewGen failed after retry 13 | SaveFieldLegacyExtended Failed 11 (11/11 System.Exception "Failed to generate view CustomAgenda|CustomEventSchedule after retry" @ ViewService.EditView:394). That's this entry's exact signature, not ki-2026-07-02 (0 FieldTableNameRef hits) or ki-2026-07-11 (no NRE).
  • ES `fields.AdditionalMetaData.MethodName:fnCreateViewFromTableName` 14:00-15:10Z: 60 records / 12 traces, 100% DatabaseName=camcraigconsulting
  • Upstream trigger traces: 6b05a301… (14:45:21Z), 6b05a653… (14:59:32Z): AlterTableToAddColumn Failed → Failed to create dropdown table! → DROP COLUMN rollback failed
  • Hypothesis, not verified vs prod (repo ref stale 07-06, GH 403): FieldService.AddDropDownFieldWithRollBack builds the child key column as Text with dropdownField.Size. An oversized/MAX size gives a non-indexable nvarchar, and the partial rollback leaves orphaned spider rows.

Suggested next action: data fix for camcraigconsulting (remove the orphaned spiderColumns/spiderViewFields rows for CustomAgendaType/CustomAgendaStatus on CustomAgenda and CustomEventScheduleType on CustomEventSchedule, or add the missing physical columns, then regenerate the views). Also file a defect: validate dropdown key size before DDL, and make the rollback also remove the parent-table metadata.

Source alerts (2 total, degraded cycle, no Slack permalinks):
  • DD monitor 299251404 Warn 14:43:24Z (recovered 14:47:24Z)
  • DD monitor 299251404 re-Warn 15:01:24Z

Evidence:

  • DD metrics: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet_core.request.errors&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cservice%3Atables-fields&exp_group=resource_name&exp_agg=sum&start=1795528800&end=1795532880
  • Kibana (74 hits): https://logstash.method.me/app/discover#/?_g=(time:(from:'2026-11-24T14:35:00Z',to:'2026-11-24T15:10:00Z'))&_a=(query:(language:kuery,query:'fields.dd_service.keyword:%22tables-fields%22%20and%20level.keyword:%22Error%22'))

  • This-window concentration: tables-fields 74 (single service, single tenant)
  • Report: docs/investigations/2026-11-24-e70607ff07926223.md

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 8)
Channel: alert-runtime-monitoring + alert-system  •  bug-type guess: code  •  alerts in group: 3
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (`@admin` / `#team-admin`) — mobile-notifications-stack per ownership.md

*Twilio bulk-SMS callback burst — 4th bot-seen fire, largest yet, now cross-channel.*

Symptoms (15:15–15:40Z, all queried this cycle):
  - 312 `POST /v1/sms/notification` → 922 Twilio `POST /v1/sms/status` callbacks on method-mobile-notifications-api
  - 92 Redis HMGET timeouts in one 5m bucket, 100% `method-mobile-notifications-api` (227940275 threshold 10, ratio 8.2); vs 45 on 11-23
  - 37 × 500 on `/v1/sms/status`, relayed 1:1 by gateway as `/mobilenotifications/sms/status` (70171778)
  - NEW: `[CRM][P1]` error-rate monitor 303750154 also tripped (Warn), first cross-channel fire of this class
  - NEW: the *send* path is hit too: `TwilioSmsProvider.ValidateAsync` → `DistributedCacheExtensions.TryGetValue` (sync `IDistributedCache.Get`), not only the callback logger

Trace IDs: 6b04545a00000000938701932e99010a
Likely cause: sync Redis `Get` on the request thread starves the .NET thread pool under the callback burst (WORKER Busy=21 vs Min=4, `mgr: 10 of 10 available`, conn-sec ~12.5d → not a Redis-server problem, no restart). Plus 6 Twilio `RequestValidator` "Concurrent operations from multiple threads" CryptographicExceptions (shared validator instance).
Chronic: mobile-notif Redis errors appear in the bulk-send hour on *every weekday 11-17 → 11-24* (hourly: 21, 2, 68+43, 9+24, 45, 92). No KB match (4 runtime-core/ms-account Redis entries refuted by the by-service breakdown).
Suggested next action: file defect (make `CacheMapperProvider.Get` / `TwilioSmsProvider.ValidateAsync` async or raise MinThreads; don't share `RequestValidator`). Ben: still pending from 11-23, should I seed `ki-…-mobile-notifications-twilio-callback-burst` so weekday repeats get KIR-suppressed, or keep it escalating until a defect exists?
